questions.question: How many coordinate axes exist in a 3D workspace (unlike 2D flat stages)?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The 3D space adds depth to width and height, introducing X, Y, and Z axes.

questions.question: Which axis represents the depth or distance (how far or close an object is to the screen) in a 3D editor?
questions.explanation: Correct! The Z-axis controls depth, making sprites appear near or far away.

questions.question: Which axis represents horizontal width movement (left and right) on a coordinate grid?
questions.explanation: Excellent! The X-axis represents horizontal motion (left/right).

questions.question: Which axis represents vertical height movement (up and down) on the stage grid?
questions.explanation: Great! The Y-axis represents vertical motion (up/down).

questions.question: What happens if we scale a 3D object to X=2, Y=2, Z=2?
options: It doubles in size across all dimensions
questions.explanation: Perfect! Scaling by 2 doubles the width, height, and depth, making the object twice as big!

questions.question: What component determines what view of the 3D world is currently displayed on screen?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The virtual Camera defines the viewer's eye position and look-direction.

questions.question: Which block is called to force the camera to keep focusing or looking at a specific moving sprite?
questions.explanation: Excellent! The 'camera look at' block automatically pivots the camera view to trace the target sprite.

questions.question: What does XR stand for in modern immersive gaming?
questions.explanation: Correct! Extended Reality includes Virtual, Augmented, and Mixed realities under one hood.

questions.question: If you want to move the camera forward towards the scene, which camera command is used?
questions.explanation: Great! The 'move camera forward' block pushes the camera viewpoint along its depth path.

questions.question: What block is used to set the initial X, Y, Z coordinate positions of a 3D sprite?
questions.explanation: Perfect! The 'set 3D position' block positions a sprite precisely in the three-dimensional space.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write 3D block pseudo-code to position a sprite at X=50, Y=100, Z=-200.
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Placing coordinates correctly distributes sprites accurately in depth and height.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write 3D block pseudo-code to make the virtual camera look at a sprite named 'HeroCar'.
questions.explanation: Perfect! Snapping this block focuses the user's view directly on the player's car!
